newsitem.title: USA: IBM soars on Salomon Brothers upgrade.
newsitem.headline: IBM soars on Salomon Brothers upgrade.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp soared after John Jones at Salomon Brothers, an influential analyst on IBM, raised his rating on the stock to a strong buy from buy, with a 12-month target of $145.

Jones said in a report to clients that in the second quarter, IBM produced the best revenue acceleration of the past five quarters and that the outlook for the second half and for 1997 is very positive.
Shares of IBM soared 3-1/2 to 115-1/4 in active trading.
"Every major product line in IBM's arsenal will have had a major refresh by September 10, when the CMOS-based mainframe is announced," Jones said in a note to clients.

Jones said that IBM is refreshing virtually all of IBM's major product families, starting a year ago with the upgrade of its AS/400 minicomputer line and concluding with the September 10 mainframe announcement.
There have also been upgrades to the RS/6000 workstation line, server families, a refresh of high-end storage systems and a rebuilding of the IBM PC Co, Jones pointed out.

"All major product families are new and healthy," Jones said. "They should help drive revenue growth at or above the June quarter run rate of nine percent (measured on a constant currency basis) for the next three to four quarters."
He said his outlook for the second half of 1996 is for good year-over-year earnings growth, with most of it coming from the fourth quarter.

"We expect the momentum to continue in 1997 with earnings growth of 18 percent," Jones said. He said that there is a possibility for more upside potential due to continued share repurchases not included in his 1997 estimates.
